'''Matthias Flach''' is a [[Germans|German]] [[mathematician]], [[professor]] and former executive officer for mathematics (department chair) at [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ratemyprofessors.com/ShowRatings.jsp?tid=461802|title=Matthias Flach at California Institute of Technology - RateMyProfessors.com|publisher=|accessdate=18 March 2016|archive-date=28 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160328004911/http://www.ratemyprofessors.com/ShowRatings.jsp?tid=461802|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name = mf>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.caltech.edu/people/flach.html|title=Matthias Flach|publisher=|accessdate=18 March 2016|archive-date=3 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303172251/http://www.math.caltech.edu/people/flach.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Professional overview==
Research interests includes:<ref name = mf />
*Arithmetic [[algebraic geometry]] (see [[Glossary of arithmetic and Diophantine geometry]]).
*[[Special values of L-functions]].
*[[Conjectures]] of:
**[[André Bloch (mathematician)|Bloch]]
**[[Alexander Beilinson|Beilinson]]
**[[Pierre Deligne|Deligne]]
**[[Bloch–Kato conjecture]] (see also [[List of conjectures]]).
*[[Galois module]] theory.
*[[Motivic cohomology]].

==Education overview==
*Ph.D. [[University of Cambridge]] UK 1991 Dissertation: [[Selmer group]]s for the [[Symmetric algebra|Symmetric Square]] of an [[Elliptic Curve]] – Algebraic geometry <ref>{{cite web|url=http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=71484|title=The Mathematics Genealogy Project - Matthias Flach|publisher=|accessdate=18 March 2016}}</ref>
*Diplom, [[Goethe University Frankfurt]], [[Germany]], 1986

==Publications==
*[[Iwasawa theory|Iwasawa Theory]] and Motivic L-functions (2009) – Flach, Matthias
*On [[Galois theory|Galois structure]] invariants associated to [[Tate motive#Geometric realizations|Tate motives]] – Matthias Flach and D. Burns, [[King's College London]]<ref>{{Cite web| title=On Galois structure invariants associated to Tate motives | url=http://www.math.caltech.edu/papers/m2.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716084533/http://www.math.caltech.edu/papers/m2.pdf | archive-date=2011-07-16}}</ref>
*On the [[Equivariant Tamagawa Number Conjecture]] for Tate Motives, Part II. (2006) – Burns, David; Flach, Matthias.
*[[Euler characteristic]]s in relative [[K-theory|K-groups]] – Matthias Flach<ref>{{Cite web| title=Euler characteristics in relative K-groups | url=http://www.math.caltech.edu/papers/euler.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000823173656/http://www.math.caltech.edu:80/papers/euler.pdf | archive-date=2000-08-23}}</ref>
*The [[equivariant]] [[Adelic algebraic group|Tamagawa number]] conjecture: A survey (with an appendix by [[Cornelius Greither|C. Greither]]) – Matthias Flach<ref>{{Cite web| url=http://www.dpmms.cam.ac.uk/Seminars/Kuwait/abstracts/L56.pdf | title=The Tamagawa Number Conjecture | access-date=2009-07-31 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140219132342/https://www.dpmms.cam.ac.uk/Seminars/Kuwait/abstracts/L56.pdf | archive-date=2014-02-19 | url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| title=The Equivariant Tamagawa Number Conjecture: A survey | url=http://www.math.caltech.edu/papers/baltimore-final.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716084547/http://www.math.caltech.edu/papers/baltimore-final.pdf | archive-date=2011-07-16}}</ref>
*A geometric example of non-[[Abelian extension|abelian]] [[Iwasawa theory]], June 2004, Canadian [[Number Theory]] Association VIII Meeting – Flach, Matthias.
*The [[Tsuneo Tamagawa|Tamagawa]] number conjecture of adjoint motives of [[modular forms]] (2004) – Diamond, Fred; Flach, Matthias; Guo, Li.
*Adjoint motives of modular forms and the Tamagawa number conjecture (2001) – [[Fred Diamond]]; Matthias Flach; Li Guo.
